prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py runs json.loads() on any string input whose field annotation isn't literally `str`, including `str | None` unions. If the string value happens to be valid JSON (e.g. a numeric-looking string, or a JSON object/array literal passed intentionally as a plain string), it gets silently converted to the wrong type, corrupting the input. Both PRs patch the same `pre_parse_json` gate in the same file/function to stop this for str-containing unions. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py runs json.loads() on any string input whose field annotation isn't literally `str`, including `str | None` unions. If the string value happens to be valid JSON (e.g. a numeric-looking string, or a JSON object/array literal passed intentionally as a plain string), it gets silently converted to the wrong type, corrupting the input. Both PRs patch the same `pre_parse_json` gate in the same file/function to stop this for str-containing unions. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3056's `_is_optional_str` narrowly targets `str | None` (the actual reported corruption case) and explicitly still allows JSON pre-parsing for other str unions like `str | list[str]` where decoding is required for correctness; it also unwraps `Annotated[...]` on individual union members, covering the common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter style. 2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead lumps str with int/float/bool into one 'simple types' set and skips pre-parsing for any union composed solely of those types (e.g. `str | int`, `str | float`), which changes behavior for unions where numeric-string-to-number coercion via JSON decoding was previously working and desired — a broader, less-scoped change than the bug it's fixing. 2032 also does not unwrap `Annotated` when checking the union origin, so it misses the `Annotated[...] | None` shape that 3056 handles.

clusters.pick_reason: 3056's `_is_optional_str` narrowly targets `str | None` (the actual reported corruption case) and explicitly still allows JSON pre-parsing for other str unions like `str | list[str]` where decoding is required for correctness; it also unwraps `Annotated[...]` on individual union members, covering the common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter style. 2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead lumps str with int/float/bool into one 'simple types' set and skips pre-parsing for any union composed solely of those types (e.g. `str | int`, `str | float`), which changes behavior for unions where numeric-string-to-number coercion via JSON decoding was previously working and desired — a broader, less-scoped change than the bug it's fixing. 2032 also does not unwrap `Annotated` when checking the union origin, so it misses the `Annotated[...] | None` shape that 3056 handles.

clusters.pick_reason: 3056's `_is_optional_str` narrowly targets `str | None` (the actual reported corruption case) and explicitly still allows JSON pre-parsing for other str unions like `str | list[str]` where decoding is required for correctness; it also unwraps `Annotated[...]` on individual union members, covering the common `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None` parameter style. 2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` instead lumps str with int/float/bool into one 'simple types' set and skips pre-parsing for any union composed solely of those types (e.g. `str | int`, `str | float`), which changes behavior for unions where numeric-string-to-number coercion via JSON decoding was previously working and desired — a broader, less-scoped change than the bug it's fixing. 2032 also does not unwrap `Annotated` when checking the union origin, so it misses the `Annotated[...] | None` shape that 3056 handles.

members.author: Bartok9
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs edit the same conditional in validate_tool_use_result_messages (src/mcp/server/validation.py) that governs what happens when a previous tool_use has no matching tool_result in the following message. They are not complementary variants of the same fix — they implement opposite behavior for the identical scenario. #2962 wraps the mismatch check in `has_tool_results and ...` so that a tool_use with zero following tool_results no longer raises at all, citing SEP-1577 (tool_result must follow tool_use, not the reverse) and adding a regression test asserting validate_tool_use_result_messages does NOT raise in that case. #3053 keeps the original raise path and adds an explicit `if not has_tool_results: raise ValueError(...)` so the same scenario still raises, just with a clearer message, and its test asserts validate_tool_use_result_messages DOES raise. Applying both is impossible: #2962's added test would fail under #3053's behavior and vice versa. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs implement essentially the same quote-aware, comma-splitting tokenizer for the WWW-Authenticate header (compare _iter_www_auth_params in #3012 vs _split_www_authenticate_segments in #3041 — same escape/quote-tracking loop). #3041 goes further by adding _extract_bearer_auth_params, which partitions each comma-segment on the scheme keyword and scopes extraction to only the Bearer challenge's params, stopping at the next scheme boundary. #3012's tokenizer only finds the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of params, so it does not correctly handle a WWW-Authenticate header containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm=..., Bearer realm=...'), a case #3041 explicitly handles.
